legibility: Kenyon 1893 (typeset, with special sorts for the signs) and Wessely 1888/1893 (typeset) are sharp at 300-600 ppi; every sign in the crops is complete. Preisendanz 1928 is a camera scan (360 ppi) of a photo-offset page; legible. Eitrem's plates are halftone collotypes of the papyrus: forms are legible but stroke ends, small rings and faint signs are blurred by the screen and papyrus fibres - transcriptions of plates VII, VIII, XI and XII are provisional. Wünsch's drawings are clear but are his freehand copies.
problems: Preisendanz PGM II (1931), which holds PGM VII and XXXVI, could not be used: the only archive.org copy is the 1973-74 second edition, access-restricted; the 1931 first edition enters the US public domain on 1 January 2027.

The British Museum photographic Facsimiles (portfolio issued with Kenyon vols. I-III, 1893) were not found; Kenyon's and Wessely's typeset sign forms are editors' approximations, not traces of the papyrus.
PGM IV 409-433: the only print found with these signs is Wessely 1888, laid out sideways; sign orientation must be checked against the manuscript (BnF suppl. gr. 574, fol. 6v).

Kenyon prints scribal abbreviation symbols in the same line as charaktêres (⍏ = δεῖνα, □ = ὄνομα, □□ = ὀνόματα, and symbols for ἥλιος and σελήνη: Index of Symbols, pp. 251-2). The tracer must not draw these as charaktêres; for VII 196 the papyrus's own count (11) suggests that the two ⍏-shaped forms there ARE counted among the charaktêres.

HathiTrust page images are blocked from this environment (HTTP 403 "Blocked from HathiTrust"); the search budget was exhausted before Gallica (BnF suppl. gr. 574) or the British Library could be located.

Archive.org page-number metadata is unreliable for the Kenyon scan (its page_numbers.json is off by 5 here) and the hOCR page index of PGM I is offset by one leaf; every printed page given here was read from the image itself.
